column1: # The Midjourney subject each item mark is generated from, so a regeneration
# matches, and a short note for the mark's own header.
# `mj-prompts.mjs` wraps each subject as "an icon of <subject>, <style>", and
# the style tail is the same for every mark — the one the class sigils and the
# domain marks read as. The subject is the only thing that varies, so it says
# what is in the picture and nothing about how it is drawn.
# One archetype each, so no two marks share a silhouette. Where count is the
# cue it is the only difference: one spearhead against two, one vial against
# `Pick` is which of the four Midjourney variants (1–4) was traced. `Job` is
# the Midjourney job it came from, so the exact art can be fetched again.

column2: Subject
a heritage emblem, two interlocking lozenges braided into a lineage knot with roots twining beneath
column5: A knot over roots: two lineages bound, and where they come from.

column2: a community emblem, a cluster of three separate small heraldic heater shields, one above and two below, edges almost touching, each shield with a carved chevron
column5: Three is the smallest count that reads as a group rather than a pair.

column2: a transformation emblem, a cracked chrysalis lozenge splitting open down its spine with swirling flame-like wings unfurling out of it
column5: One thing breaking open into another.

column2: a war banner emblem, a pennant flag on a spear staff, its cloth cut into a deep swallow-tail and rippling
column5: The standard you fight under. Only drawn where a homebrew class's domain sigil cannot resolve.

column2: a branching emblem, a heavy stem forking into two tapering curved arms each ending in a hooked point, like a split antler
column5: A branch: a subclass is one of the ways a class goes.

column2: a tarot card emblem, a tall upright card with cut corners and a pierced diamond star at its centre
column5: The card's own silhouette with its sigil voided.

column2: a rank chevron emblem, a broad upward chevron with barbed tapering tips crowned by a small four-pointed star
column5: The charge for something earned and held.

column2: a spearhead emblem, a single broad leaf spearhead point up with swept barbed shoulders and a socket
column5: A point is the one weapon idea that is not also a genre.

column2: a twin spearhead emblem, two slender spearheads side by side points up, shoulders swept outward
column5: The same idea twice: the secondary slot is where a second weapon goes.

column2: a knight helm emblem, a crested great helm with a visor slit and flared cheek guards, front view
column5: A helm rather than a torso, so the generic armour mark is not mistaken for plate.

column2: a trio of small bottles emblem, three stoppered vials of different heights clustered together
column5: Three bottles, so it never reads as the single-vial or potion marks.

column2: a buckled strap emblem, a crossed pair of leather straps with an ornate square buckle and diamond boss at the centre
